title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page finishes a sentence begun on the previous page. Grothendieck works with the Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen compactification \hat M_{g,ν} of the moduli stack of ν-pointed genus-g curves. He uses 'MD-graphes', which are stable dual graphs. For each such graph G he has a closed stratum \hat M_{[G]}, and also its rigidified version (\hat M_G, Γ^!), where Γ^! is the subgroup of Aut(G) acting trivially on the marked points.

The previous page states the combinatorics. If G has M edges, its 2^M generalizations are the contractions along subsets of edges. These correspond bijectively to the closed strata \hat M_{[G']} that contain \hat M_{[G]}. These strata are proper and smooth over Z. Any generalization morphism of écart δ factors into écart-1 steps in δ! ways.

This page draws the conclusion. Read in modern terms, the passage is: 'This is the typical situation of a structure at infinity with normal crossings. The local analysis near a given generalized MD-curve (X̂, I), over an algebraically closed field (reading uncertain), by means of formal modular schemes shows that this really is a normal-crossings situation. We will come back to this later.'

In modern language: the boundary \hat M_{g,ν} \ M_{g,ν} is a relative normal-crossings divisor over Spec Z. Its strata are indexed by stable graphs. A stratum of codimension M lies in exactly M local branches of the boundary, one per node. The proof meant is the deformation-theoretic one. The formal (universal) deformation space of a stable curve with M nodes is a formal power series ring in 3g-3+ν variables over W(k) or Z. In it, the locus where the i-th node persists is {t_i = 0}, with the t_i (i = 1, …, M) part of a coordinate system.

The point serves the programme of the manuscript: describing the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν}, i.e. its stratified boundary and the tubular neighbourhoods of strata. The next page begins the case-by-case study of the strata of dimension ≤ 2.
errors: No mathematical error. The normal-crossings claim is asserted here and deferred ('on y reviendra'), not proved on this page.

The divisor is normal crossings only in the stack sense (strictly speaking only étale-locally / on the stack). On coarse spaces, or for graphs with self-loops, the branches are not globally distinct components. Grothendieck's distinction between \hat M_{[G]} and the rigidified (\hat M_G, Γ^!) is precisely the device for handling this.

ideas.what: Boundary of the compactified moduli stack \hat M_{g,ν} is a (relative) normal-crossings divisor over Z, with strata indexed by stable graphs; closed strata containing a given stratum correspond to subsets of the edges (2^M of them).
ideas.modern_name: Normal crossings boundary of \bar M_{g,n}; stratification by stable dual graphs
ideas.where_published: The idea of studying M_{g,ν} 'at infinity' via stable-graph strata and tubular neighbourhoods is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this precise statement is not, to my knowledge, there.

ideas.what: Proof by local analysis of formal (universal) deformations of a stable curve: node-smoothing parameters as part of a coordinate system.
ideas.modern_name: Deformation theory of nodal curves; local structure of \bar M_{g,n} near the boundary

deep.surprise_reason: Short concluding sentence asserting the well-known normal-crossings structure of the Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen boundary, with the proof deferred; standard since 1969.
transcription_corrections: 'au voisinage d'une {+MD-+}courbe' — the superscript 'MD-' is inserted before 'courbe', giving 'MD-courbe généralisée'.
'l'analyse locale {+de[?]+}' — the small inserted mark is probably a stray 'de' or 'à'; the phrase reads 'l'analyse locale au voisinage'.
'(sur un corps de [?])' — plausibly '(sur un corps alg. clos)'; reading uncertain.
'à coups des' should be read as 'à coups de', i.e. 'by means of'.
'montre que – bel et bien, une telle situation' — likely 'montre que c'est bel et bien une telle situation'.
'schémas modulaires [-local-] formels' — the struck word is 'local'; the final text is 'schémas modulaires formels'.
